faqs.question: What are the most popular Halloween meme formats?
faqs.answer: The ones that return every year: spooky season starting on 1 September, kid-you versus adult-you, costume expectation versus reality, the last-minute costume, the candy ranking, the waiting skeleton, spooky versus cosy, the 1 November Christmas switch and the 'please take one' candy bowl. faqs.question: What do I need to make a funny Halloween meme?
faqs.answer: Only a phone. Pick a familiar format, use a photo you took, and put a short setup on top and the twist at the bottom. Bold white text with a dark outline stays readable on any photo.

faqs.question: How long should a meme caption be?
faqs.answer: Aim for under about 8 words per line and two lines in total. Memes are mostly seen on phones, and on SubhSandesh 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so long captions get cut off or skipped.

faqs.question: Is it legal to use movie screenshots in memes?
faqs.answer: It depends. The U.S. Copyright Office says courts weigh four factors, including whether the use is commercial and how much of the work is used, and there is no formula that makes a set amount safe. Sharing with friends is low risk; using a film still to sell something is the riskiest.

faqs.question: Are memes covered by fair use?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Fair use is decided case by case on the four factors in Section 107 of the U.S. Copyright Act, so a meme made from someone else's image may or may not qualify. Using your own photo with your own caption avoids the question.

faqs.question: Why is candy corn always in Halloween memes?
faqs.answer: Because people split sharply on it, and a divisive food invites replies. Google's Frightgeist 2025 even listed 'dill pickle candy corn' as a breakout search, which became its own joke.

faqs.question: Why is the giant skeleton a Halloween meme?
faqs.answer: The 12-foot skeleton went viral in 2020 and, according to Google's Frightgeist 2025 round-up, has stayed a top trending Halloween decor search since. Its size makes it an easy visual exaggeration.

faqs.question: What makes a meme relatable rather than just funny?
faqs.answer: Researchers treat them as separate judgements. In a 2026 study of 225 adults, Jach and colleagues found procrastination memes were rated the most relatable, which is why the last-minute costume joke travels so well.

faqs.question: Can I send a Halloween meme as a personal card?
faqs.answer: Yes. Put your caption in the letter on the /happy-halloween page and add up to six photos; the recipient walks through a little haunted house, carves a pumpkin and reads your letter by flashlight. It is a one-person page, not a group-chat tool.

faqs.question: Are these Halloween meme captions safe for kids and work?
faqs.answer: Yes. All 36 captions on this page are clean and aim the joke at the season or at yourself rather than at a named person. For family and kids, the spooky-versus-cosy format is the gentlest.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Memes: 9 Formats and 36 Captions to Make Your Own

Halloween memes are a small set of formats that return every October: spooky season starting in September, the costume that looked better online, the candy ranking, the giant skeleton and the 1 November switch to Christmas. Most get opened on a phone. On SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone and the average shared page collects 11.1 views. Those are platform-wide figures, not Halloween ones, but they set two rules for funny Halloween memes: the text must read on a small screen, and a good one gets passed around.

Below are the 9 formats described in words, 36 original top-and-bottom captions for your own photos, a five-step method using tools already on your phone, and what the U.S. Copyright Office says about using other people's images.

## What is a Halloween meme?

A Halloween meme is a picture with a caption that reuses a joke template people already recognise, applied to costumes, candy or the season. The classic shape is the [image macro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_macro): one image, top text that sets up, bottom text that lands.

The set is stable because the calendar is: Halloween is always 31 October. Google's [Frightgeist 2025 round-up](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/frightgeist-2025/) (9 October 2025) said the 12-foot skeleton "continues to be a top trending search ever since it went viral in 2020", and named "dill pickle candy corn" a breakout search. Both are meme material.

## 9 Halloween meme formats that return every October

Every caption is original and clean. Each format gets three notes: picture, why it works, who to send it to.

### 1. Spooky season starts 1 September

**Picture:** decorations going up in obvious summer weather. **Why it works:** it teases the early starter, who laughs loudest. **Send to:** the friend with more skeletons than mugs.

- Top: "It's 1 September" / Bottom: "So basically October"
- Top: "Me putting up a pumpkin" / Bottom: "In shorts and sunscreen"
- Top: "Summer isn't over" / Bottom: "Says someone without a cauldron"
- Top: "Countdown to Halloween" / Bottom: "Day 61. Still counting"

### 2. Two Halloweens: kid you vs adult you

**Picture:** a child with an overflowing candy bag beside a tired adult on the sofa. **Why it works:** everyone has lived both halves. **Send to:** siblings and school friends.

- Top: "Kid me: 4 hours, 3 streets, 1 pillowcase" / Bottom: "Adult me: buys the bag, eats the bag"
- Top: "At 9, Halloween was a sport" / Bottom: "At 29, it's a nap in a cape"
- Top: "Then: knock on every door" / Bottom: "Now: hide from every knock"
- Top: "Kid me traded candy like stocks" / Bottom: "Adult me just wants the good chocolate"

### 3. Costume expectation vs reality

**Picture:** the inspiration photo next to your homemade attempt. **Why it works:** it is self-mocking, so nobody gets hurt. **Send to:** the group chat on 1 November.

- Top: "The costume I ordered" / Bottom: "The costume that arrived"
- Top: "Going as a fierce witch" / Bottom: "Arrived as a damp hat"
- Top: "The tutorial said 20 minutes" / Bottom: "The tutorial lied"
- Top: "Expectation: glamorous vampire" / Bottom: "Reality: tired person with ketchup"

### 4. The costume at 6 p.m. on 31 October

**Picture:** someone wrapped in a bedsheet or toilet paper. **Why it works:** it is a procrastination joke, the kind research below found most relatable. **Send to:** the friend who says "I'll figure it out".

- Top: "Planning my costume since August" / Bottom: "Making it at 6:15 p.m. on the day"
- Top: "Is it a ghost costume" / Bottom: "Or did I lose a fight with a duvet"
- Top: "I'm a mummy" / Bottom: "I had one roll of tape and a dream"
- Top: "My costume is 'person who forgot'" / Bottom: "Very convincing"

### 5. Candy ranking and the candy corn debate

**Picture:** a tier list, or candy corn held at arm's length. **Why it works:** everyone has an opinion, so it invites replies. **Send to:** whoever will argue back.

- Top: "Candy corn haters" / Bottom: "Candy corn lovers. Both very loud"
- Top: "Someone made dill pickle candy corn" / Bottom: "And chose chaos"
- Top: "Raisins in my trick-or-treat bag" / Bottom: "The real horror story"
- Top: "Me judging the candy haul" / Bottom: "Chocolate: guilty of being delicious"

### 6. The skeleton who waited

**Picture:** a skeleton slumped on a bench, or the 12-foot one towering over a house. **Why it works:** it exaggerates waiting. **Send to:** someone running late.

- Top: "Me waiting for your reply" / Bottom: "Since last Halloween"
- Top: "Waiting for the group to pick a costume" / Bottom: "Still waiting"
- Top: "The 12-foot skeleton" / Bottom: "Taller than my patience"
- Top: "The neighbours bought a giant skeleton" / Bottom: "We live in its shadow now"

### 7. Spooky vs cosy

**Picture:** a sweet ghost in a blanket, or a cat in a witch hat. **Why it works:** cute-strange images seem to appeal more under stress. **Send to:** a partner, a parent, anyone who hates horror films.

- Top: "My Halloween plan" / Bottom: "Blanket, tea, one very small ghost"
- Top: "I'm spooky" / Bottom: "Between 7 and 9 p.m. only"
- Top: "Horror movie night?" / Bottom: "Cartoon pumpkins only, thanks"
- Top: "Tiny ghost says boo" / Bottom: "Then apologises"

### 8. The 1 November Christmas switch

**Picture:** a shop aisle where pumpkins give way to tinsel. **Why it works:** it happens every year, so it never dates. **Send to:** the Christmas person and the Halloween person.

- Top: "11:59 p.m., 31 October" / Bottom: "12:00 a.m.: is that jingle bells?"
- Top: "Halloween isn't even cold yet" / Bottom: "Santa already moved in"
- Top: "Me on 1 November" / Bottom: "Still in fangs, buying discount candy"
- Top: "Skeleton in a Santa hat" / Bottom: "Seasonal multitasking"

### 9. The "please take one" candy bowl

**Picture:** an empty bowl beside a hopeful sign. **Why it works:** it pokes fun at the honour system without naming anyone. **Send to:** neighbours and parents.

- Top: "Sign: please take one" / Bottom: "Bowl: empty in 4 minutes"
- Top: "Kid me at the 'take one' bowl" / Bottom: "Define one"
- Top: "Left candy out on the honour system" / Bottom: "Learned about honour"
- Top: "Last kid of the night" / Bottom: "Gets the bowl, the sign and my respect"

## Why some funny Halloween memes land and others flop

Funny and relatable are separate judgements. In a 2026 study of 225 adults, [Jach and colleagues in Current Issues in Personality Psychology](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13392671) had people rate memes about everyday struggles for funniness and for how well each matched their own situation; procrastination memes were the most relatable. That is why format 4 travels.

A second 2026 paper, [An and colleagues in Behavioral Sciences](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13603214), surveyed 356 adults and ran an experiment with 393. People asked to recall something stressful rated "ugly-cute" images more favourably and chose them more often, which fits the pull of format 7.

- **Aim the joke at yourself or the season.** A joke about a named friend's costume can sting.
- **Keep each line under about 8 words.** It has to survive a phone screen.

## How to make a Halloween meme in 5 steps

Any phone photo editor or text-on-image tool works. You need no special app or account.

1. **Pick one of the 9 formats.** A familiar shape does half the work.
2. **Use a photo you took.** Your cat in a cape is funnier and sidesteps copyright questions.
3. **Top line sets up, bottom line twists.** If it needs a third line, cut words.
4. **Use bold white text with a dark outline.** It reads on light and dark photos.
5. **Check it on your phone first.** With 48.3% of SubhSandesh views on a phone and 48.4% on a touch device, assume a small screen.

## Can you get in trouble for using meme images?

Possibly, if the photo, film still or artwork belongs to someone else. The U.S. Copyright Office's [fair-use guidance](https://www.copyright.gov/fair-use/more-info.html) lists 4 factors courts weigh: purpose and character of the use, nature of the original, how much was used, and the effect on the original's market. It adds there is "no formula" making any set amount safe.

- **Sharing with friends** is the lowest-risk use, but not automatically fair use.
- **Using a film still to sell something** is the riskiest: commercial use and creative source material both weigh against you.
- **Your own photo plus your own caption** avoids the question.

The Office gives no individual legal advice. Businesses should ask a lawyer.

## Meme, story or personal page: which suits the person?

This compares four ways to send a Halloween joke. SubhSandesh's platform-wide figures appear where they exist.

| Option | Who sees it | Time and size | SubhSandesh data (all templates) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group-chat meme | Everyone in one chat | 2–5 minutes, one square image | Not measured |
| Story meme | Your followers, for 24 hours | 2–5 minutes, one 9:16 image | Not measured |
| /happy-halloween page | One person | About 5 minutes, up to 6 photos | 11.1 average views per page |
| /happy-halloween-premium page | One person | About 10 minutes, up to 12 photos and a 60-second voice note | 90.9% of started pages get published |

Memes win on speed and reach. A page wins for one person.

## When a meme beats a personal page

For a group chat, a meme is better. SubhSandesh's Halloween pages are one-person greeting pages, not party tools, in English only, and someone wanting a 10-second laugh may not want a haunted house.

If the meme is really for one person, the [interactive Halloween card at /happy-halloween](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is the next step. Put your best caption in the letter, add up to six photos, and they knock three times, carve a pumpkin and read your letter by flashlight. It ends with "Will you be my boo?" (or a bestie, family or kids version), emails you when they first answer, and gives them a 1080×1920 Boo License to download.

The [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds a voice note up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos and an optional unlock time. Platform-wide, 90.9% of started pages are published and shared.

## Sources

- U.S. Copyright Office, [More Information on Fair Use](https://www.copyright.gov/fair-use/more-info.html), undated.
- Google, [Frightgeist 2025](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/frightgeist-2025/), 9 October 2025.
- Jach et al., [funniness ratings of memes](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13392671), 11 June 2026.
- An et al., [ugly–cute meme preference](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13603214), 4 September 2026.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Every page in the US top 10 is an image gallery (Bored Panda ~30 images, AOL 50, Yahoo 73) with no format explanations, no make-your-own method and no copyright guidance; this is the only text-first page, with 36 original captions, two 2026 open-access meme studies and copyright.gov's fair-use factors, which is what an answer engine can actually lift. But the query is image-intent: Google will keep favouring galleries and Pinterest for the head term, and a text page with no images and a young domain should expect to win AI answers and long-tail 'how to make a halloween meme' / 'are memes fair use' queries before it wins 'halloween memes' itself.
